request_body.raw_goal: Learn to paint with watercolors. I've always wanted to try.
request_body.user_context: Recently retired schoolteacher, Portland. Widowed two years ago. No deadlines, no career pressure. Wants structure and purpose, not achievement targets. Low weekly hours — this is how she likes it.

objectives: Develop foundational knowledge of watercolor pigment properties and paper interaction.
Master essential brush manipulation techniques for controlling water-to-paint ratios.
Practice core application methods including wet-on-wet, wet-on-dry, and color glazing.
Cultivate a consistent, low-pressure creative practice that emphasizes personal enjoyment.

proposed_milestones.description: Establish a basic watercolor workstation and learn paper preparation techniques.
objectives: Select and source fundamental supplies: cold-press paper, student-grade tube paints, and round synthetic brushes.
Practice stretching paper to understand how it reacts to water saturation.
Organize a simple palette to ensure colors are accessible for short sessions.

proposed_milestones.description: Master brush control and water-to-pigment ratio consistency.
objectives: Create a series of value scales using a single pigment to learn pigment density.
Practice basic brush strokes—flat, graded, and variegated washes—to observe how paint moves on wet paper.
Understand the 'bead' of paint and how to guide it across the surface without streaking.

proposed_milestones.description: Explore layering techniques to understand depth and color transparency.
objectives: Experiment with wet-on-dry layering to understand how to build depth through glazes.
Execute a simple monochromatic landscape to focus on atmospheric perspective.
Practice color mixing to create harmonious palettes rather than relying on tube colors directly.

proposed_milestones.description: Develop a recurring, low-stakes creative routine.
objectives: Complete five 'sketchbook studies' that focus on subjects of personal interest rather than technical perfection.
Reflect on completed pieces to identify preferred techniques and color preferences.
Standardize a cleanup routine that makes beginning future sessions effortless.

success_metrics: Completion of a color chart showcasing primary, secondary, and tertiary mixing outcomes.
Ability to demonstrate a smooth, consistent flat wash covering a 4x4 inch area.
Creation of a personal sketchbook containing at least 10 completed watercolor studies.
Establishment of a consistent painting rhythm that feels sustainable without external pressure.

success_metrics: Confirmed placement in a recurring weekly volunteer slot at a library branch.
